ledger.x: 587: the Lombard kingdom of King Authari continues under Cliopatria's new row.
587: the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento are drawn as the kingdom's autonomous south.
587: the Duchy of Benevento as the kingdom's autonomous south (see the Spoleto entry).

c. 603: the Lombards take Padua, Cremona, Mantua and the Po towns from the Exarchate. 'the decade up to 603' saw advances including Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Monselice, Este, Cremona and Mantua; the individual years are not on the page. Cliopatria's shape grows in 602.
628: a small southern or Friulian extension.
633: a small southern or Friulian extension.
638: a small southern or Friulian extension.
641: Rothari conquers Genoa and Oderzo.
643: Rothari completes the conquest of Liguria.
645: Rothari beats the exarch on the Scultenna.
727: Liutprand crosses the Po.
727: the war for Ravenna begins.
728: Liutprand gives Sutri to the papacy.
741: Spoleto leaves the kingdom's shape.
741: Benevento leaves the kingdom's shape (see the Spoleto entry); Cliopatria's Benevento row runs 741-749.
741: the Pentapolis and part of Umbria and Lazio fall out of the shape.
751: Aistulf takes Spoleto into his own hand.
751: Benevento is again within the kingdom's reach.
751: Aistulf takes Ravenna and the Exarchate.
751: the Exarchate falls and the Lombard-Byzantine fight for Ravenna ends.
752: Aistulf conquers the Pentapolis.
755: the shape reaches further into Lazio.
755: Pepin besieges Pavia.
756: the second Frankish campaign.
756: Pepin's gift.
763: more Emilia passes to the papacy.
773: Charlemagne marches on Pavia.
774: Pavia falls.
774: Benevento no longer the kingdom's: Cliopatria gives it its own row from 775.
June 774: Charlemagne takes the Lombard crown.

wars.name: Lombard-Frankish wars of the 580s and 590s
wars.outcome: The page lists 'Frankish wars (585, 588, 590s)' and says Authari 'drove the Franks into Piedmont' in 585; the results of 588 and the 590s are not given and Cliopatria's shape does not change in 587-601.

wars.name: Agilulf's advances against the Exarchate
wars.outcome: Lombard gains in the Po valley 'in the decade up to 603'.

wars.name: Rothari's conquest of Byzantine Liguria and Emilia
wars.outcome: Genoa and Oderzo in 641, the rest of Liguria in 643, the exarch's defeat on the Scultenna in 645; Byzantium left with 'only the Ravennan marshes in northern Italy'.

wars.name: Lombard conquest of the Exarchate of Ravenna
wars.outcome: Liutprand's 727 conquests and brief hold on Ravenna in the 730s; Aistulf takes Ravenna in 751 and the Pentapolis in 752, ending the exarchate.

wars.name: Pepin the Short's Italian campaigns against Aistulf
wars.outcome: Pepin crossed the Alps in 754 and 755, besieged Pavia in 755 and returned in 756; Aistulf paid an annual tribute and lost the Exarchate lands to the papacy.

wars.name: Desiderius' war on the papacy
wars.outcome: In 772 Adrian I demanded the surrender of territory and Desiderius 'resumed war against Romagna's cities'; in 773 Pope Hadrian 'openly broke with king Desiderius' and called in Charlemagne.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom (siege of Pavia)
wars.outcome: Charlemagne's two armies of spring 773 besieged Pavia for eight months; it fell in June 774 and the kingdom passed to Charlemagne as 'king of the Lombards'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages for the kingdom's frontier with the Exarchate, Venice, the Franks or the Bavarians; the lines of 756 (Pepin's return of the Exarchate to the pope) are described by city, not by line.
